'''Pradeep Mathur''' (born 1955) is an Indian organometallic and cluster chemist and the founder director of the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Indore]].<ref name="Director">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iiti.ac.in/administration.php |title=Director |date=2016 |publisher=IIT Indore}}</ref><ref name="Our Focus is Quality Faculty, Research Facility">{{Cite web |url=http://digitallearning.eletsonline.com/2012/12/our-focus-is-quality-faculty-research-facility/ |title=Our Focus is Quality Faculty, Research Facility |date=17 December 2012 |publisher=Digital Learning}}</ref> He is a former professor of the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Mumbai]]<ref name="Welcome to Prof. Pradeep Mathur's Homepage">{{Cite web |url=http://www.chem.iitb.ac.in/~mathur/ |title=Welcome to Prof. Pradeep Mathur's Homepage |date=2016 |publisher=IIT Mumbai}}</ref> and is known for his studies on mixed metal cluster compounds.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=183 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2016 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> He is an elected fellow of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Mathur,_Prof._Pradeep |title=Fellow profile |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 2000, for his contributions to chemical sciences.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> He has also been honoured by the award of an honorary Doctor of Science degree by the University of Keele in the U.K.

== Biography ==

Pradeep Mathur, born on 17 August 1955 in [[Teheran]] to Damyanti and Amrit Dayal. Mathur and his older brother, renowned physicist at TIFR, Deepak Mathur (married to Helen Mathur) were both brought up and educated in London whilst their father Amrit Dayal worked as a senior diplomatic official at the Indian High Commission in London and Accra. Mathur continued to live in England till he moved to Yale. He gained an honours degree at the [[University of North London]] in 1976 and secured a PhD from [[Keele University]] in 1981 before moving onto [[Yale University]] as a post-doctoral researcher.<ref name="We offer Holistic Education, Student-Centred Pedagogy - Interview with Prof Pradeep Mathur, Director IIT Indore">{{Cite web |url=http://www.engineering.careers360.com/articles/we-offer-holistic-education-student-centred-pedagogy-interview-prof-pradeep-mathur-director |title=We offer Holistic Education, Student-Centred Pedagogy - Interview with Prof Pradeep Mathur, Director IIT Indore |date=13 July 2015 |publisher=Careers 360}}</ref> Mathur chose to move  to India and joined [[Indian Institute of Technology, Mumbai]] in 1984 as a member of the faculty of chemistry where he held several positions before reaching the position of a professor<ref name="P. Mathur, Professor">{{Cite web |url=http://www.chem.iitb.ac.in/people/Faculty/prof/pm.html |title=P. Mathur, Professor |date=2016 |publisher=IIT Mumbai}}</ref> and the head of the National Single Crystal X-ray Diffraction Facility.<ref name="Welcome to Prof. Pradeep Mathur's Homepage" /> When the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Indore]] was established in 2009, Mathur was appointed as its founder director. At the end of his first five-year term, his contract was extended for a second term  and he continues to hold the position,<ref name="Director" /> simultaneously serving as a professor of the department of chemistry.<ref name="Faculty">{{Cite web |url=http://chemistry.iiti.ac.in/faculty.htm |title=Faculty |date=2016 |publisher=IIT Indore}}</ref> He has been a visiting professor at [[University of Cambridge]], [[University of Freiburg]] and [[University of Karlsruhe]] and has been associated with a number of scientific journals, viz. [[Organometallics]], Journal of Organometallic Chemistry and [[Journal of Cluster Science]] as a member of their editorial boards.<ref name="Director" />

Mathur is married to Vinita and the couple have two daughters, Nehika and Saloni.

== Legacy and honors ==
Mathur's researches were focused on the organometallic chemistry of mixed metal cluster compounds and he has developed synthetic strategies for introducing [[chalcogen]] bridges.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{Cite web |url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf |title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners |date=2016 |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research |access-date=29 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043957/http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf |archive-date=4 March 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> At IIT Mumbai, he handled projects related to the investigation of unusual metal mediated transformations and the interactions between the metal atoms and unsaturated organic species.<ref name="Summary of Achievements">{{Cite web |url=http://serb.gov.in/pdfs/research/Prof_Pradeep_Mathur.pdf |title=Summary of Achievements |date=2016 |publisher=Science and Engineering Research Board}}</ref> He has published his researches by way of chapters contributed to books authored by others<ref>{{cite book|title=Advances in Organometallic Chemistry|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cF76voG_-t4C&pg=PA243|date=23 July 1997|publisher=Academic Press|isbn=978-0-08-058042-5|pages=243–}}</ref> and over 180 peer-reviewed articles;<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Mathur=3APradeep=3A=3A.html |title=Browse by Fellow |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> [[ResearchGate]] and [[Google Scholar]], two online repositories have listed several of them.<ref name="On ResearchGate">{{Cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Pradeep_Mathur |title=On ResearchGate |date=2016 }}</ref><ref name="On Google Scholar">{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=tzaYOskAAAAJ&hl=en |title=On Google Scholar |date=2016 |publisher=Google Scholar}}</ref> He has also guided 22 doctoral scholars in their studies.<ref name="Director" />

Mathur was a [[Fulbright scholar]] in 1995<ref name="Prof. Pradeep Mathur">{{Cite web |url=https://vidwan.inflibnet.ac.in/profile/21280 |title=Prof. Pradeep Mathur |date=2016 |publisher=Vidwan |work=Web profile}}</ref> and the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] elected him as a fellow in 1996.<ref name="Fellow profile" /> The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 2000.<ref name="Chemical Sciences">{{cite web | url=http://www.csir.res.in/External/Heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm | title=Chemical Sciences | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=2016 | access-date=7 November 2016 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120912012851/http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm | archive-date=12 September 2012 }}</ref> He has also been honoured with an honorary D.Sc. degree by the University of Keele in the U.K.
